facts.text: Crestview’s rise began with the 2010 opening of the MetroRail Red Line station, instantly making the neighborhood one of Austin’s most transit‑connected spots.
The area around the new station quickly evolved into Crestview Commons, a walkable cluster of restaurants, bars, and shops that now defines the neighborhood’s downtown vibe.
The neighborhood’s streets are noted for their uniformity and charm, with mature pecan, oak, and cedar elm trees shading many of the classic ranch homes.
Crestview’s name honors the early 20th‑century developer A.B. Beddow, who built the area on the site of an old dairy farm in the 1950s and 1960s.
